question.text: If $f(x)=\int_0^{\sin ^2 x} \sin ^{-1} \sqrt{t}$ $dt$ and $g(x)=\int_0^{\cos ^2 x} \cos ^{-1} \sqrt{t}$ $dt$, then the value of $f(x)+g(x)$ is

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} \text f^{\prime}(x)+g^{\prime}(x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow f(x)+g(x)=\text { constant }(\text { say } c) \\ & \text { putting } x=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ \therefore & c=\int_0^{1 / 2}\left(\sin ^{-1} \sqrt{t}+\cos ^{-1} \sqrt{t}\right) d t=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$
